liam: FYI - saw a weird pattern this morning where streaming fncall responses triggered validator errors mid-stream and router bounced the request to async-degen, which ended up being billed. Console trace is messy.

nora: Oof. Which validator? streaming-typed-strict?

liam: Yes. Example from router: ```
2026-03-25T07:41:05Z INFO stream_chunk validator=streaming-typed-strict fncall=tool.transcribe chunk=3 status=REJECT reason=SchemaMismatch details=\"chunk.payload missing required field 'segment_id'\"
2026-03-25T07:41:05Z INFO router action=reroute target=async-degen billing_tag=charged
```

kevin: Two failure modes here: 1) validator treating per-chunk missing optional keys as fatal, 2) router lacks chunk-granular semantics and treats any mid-stream reject as full-request reroute+bill.

eva: Telemetry also aggregates only at request-level so we can't see how many chunks were soft vs hard failures. That makes triage annoying.

telemetry-bot: Suggested metric: stream_chunk_rejects_total{severity=\"soft|hard\"} and billed_rerouted_streams_total.

nora: Short term: change router policy to treat mid-stream rejects as "stream-hold" -> drop-charge + escalate to background reprocess instead of immediate billing reroute. Patch idea: ```yaml
- id: stream-midreject-handling
  match: { stream: true, event: chunk_reject }
  action: { hold: true, reroute: background-reprocess, charge: false }
```

liam: Good. I'll flip the streaming canary back off while we patch. Command: `/rollout set validator:streaming-typed-strict=soft-canary --id=st-9`

devops-bot: @liam received request to set validator:streaming-typed-strict -> soft-canary (st-9). Applying...
devops-bot: Done. 25% traffic.

kevin: I'll open the router PR and add unit tests for chunk handling and billing=false. ETA 2h.

eva: I'll add the chunk-level metrics to the streaming dashboard and create an alert: if billed_rerouted_streams_total / stream_chunk_rejects_total > 0.002 during canary, page SRE.

nora: Also we should change the validator to emit "reject_scope=chunk|request" so rules can be finer-grained. Long-term: acceptance criteria for streaming strict canaries should require chunk-level reject rate < 0.05% and zero billed reroutes for 1h.

liam: Action items: 1) liam rolled canary -> soft (done). 2) kevin PR for router policy + tests (ETA 2h). 3) eva add chunk-level telemetry & alert (ETA 4h). 4) nora spec validator reject_scope field (ETA next week).

kevin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routers/pull/5017 includes chunk-hold logic + billing unit tests.

eva: Dashboard drafts: timeseries for stream_chunk_rejects_total by severity, gauge for billed_rerouted_streams_ratio, and a table linking sample trace ids for rerouted streams.

liam: Customer impact: looks like ~420 streamed calls rerouted and billed across 2 accounts during the 30m spike. Low $$ but need CS notice if they ping.

nora: I'll update the canary playbook to include streaming caveats and add a preflight checklist item: "verify degen/async paths are non-billable for mid-stream validation failures".

telemetry-bot: Reminder: include sample retention for rerouted streams (5% for 24h) to aid debugging.

kevin: Once PR merges, we'll run the synthetic stream test that simulates missing segment_id on chunk 3 and confirm router logs show charge=false and trace includes hold->background id.

liam: Thanks team. Let's re-enable strict only after chunk-level rejects stable and billed reroute ratio < 0.01% for 1h.

eva: On it. I'll monitor while the PR lands. :thumbsup:
